description.narrative:
Insatsen består av stöd till en Challenge Fund; REACT (Renewable Energy And Climate Technologies). REACT administreras av Africa Enterprise Challenge Fund Ltd (AECF). Från och med januari 2025 genomförs projektet i Kenya och andra länder förväntas ansluta sig under loppet av 2025.
Projektets övergripande mål är att uppnå en minskning av energifattigdom, miljöförstöring och resursutarmning och bidra till ekonomisk tillväxt och ökad sysselsättning. Den förväntar sig att öka tillgången till prisvärd, hållbar och modern energi och grön teknik för hushåll och företag, vilket möjliggör förbättrade levnadsvillkor och ger ekonomiska möjligheter. Det kommer att stärka företag i tidiga skeden och växande företag inom energi- och gröntekniksektorerna genom en kombination av förmånliga finansierings- och rådgivningstjänster, främja klimatmotståndskraft, främja en cirkulär ekonomi, skydda biologisk mångfald och uppmuntra regenerativa markanvändningsmetoder. Ytterst syftar insatsen till att katalysera en rättvis energiomställning, och säkerställa att samhällen drar nytta av både ekonomisk tillväxt och miljömässig hållbarhet, där den privata sektorn spelar en central roll i att driva denna omvandling.

The contribution consists of support to a Challenge Fund; REACT (Renewable Energy And Climate Technologies). REACT is administrated by Africa Enterprise Challenge Fund Ltd (AECF). Initially from January 2025, the project is implemented in Kenya and other countries are expected to join in the course of 2025.
The overall objective of the Project is to achieve a reduction in energy poverty, environmental degradation and resource depletion and contribute to economic growth and increased employment opportunities. It expects to increase access to affordable, sustainable and modern energy and green technologies for households and businesses, enabling them to improve their living conditions and economic opportunities. It will empower early-stage and growing businesses in the energy and green-tech sectors through a combination of concessional finance and advisory services, fostering climate resilience, promoting a circular economy, protecting biodiversity, and encouraging regenerative land use practices. Ultimately, the intervention aims to catalyze a just energy transition, ensuring that communities benefit from both economic growth and environmental sustainability, with the private sector playing a central role in driving this transformation.

The contribution aims to support innovations and market development of pro-poor business models, providing underserved customers with services that drive economic growth, resilience, and climate change mitigation. The program focuses on renewable energy, e-mobility, productive use of energy, green technologies, and digital innovations for low-income households and micro enterprises. It promotes sustainable technologies that efficiently use, reuse, and recycle resources, protect ecosystems and help people adapt to climate change.
Using a challenge fund approach, the program offers seed funding through matching grants to early-stage companies and startups, helping them establish operations and attract further investment. Companies are selected through a transparent process and receive technical assistance to enhance their success. Lessons learned will inform policy development and reforms, enabling private companies to expand services to underserved customers and create sustainable impacts, reducing the need for grants over time.
The specific goals of the intervention include:
Supporting Innovations and Market Development: Promoting pro-poor business models that provide underserved customers with access to services that drive economic growth, resilience, and climate change mitigation.
Unlocking New Business Models and Technologies: Focusing on renewable energy, e-mobility, productive use of energy, clean cooking technologies, and digital innovations for low-income households and micro enterprises.
Promoting Sustainable and Clean Technologies: Encouraging the efficient use, reuse, and recycling of resources, protecting ecosystems, and helping people adapt to climate change.
Catalyzing a Just Energy Transition: Enhancing community resilience, environmental sustainability, and livelihoods through effective private sector engagement.
Providing Seed Funding and Technical Assistance: Using a challenge fund approach to support early-stage companies and startups, helping them establish operations and attract further investment.
Encouraging Policy Development and Reform: Using lessons learned to advocate for continued reform and policy development in targeted countries, enabling private companies to expand their services to underserved customers.
These goals aim to create large, impactful programs with high visibility, fostering collaboration and strategic alignment across multiple countries.
Each component of the intervention will have its specific objectives aligned with the general program aim. These objectives are based on country specific rationale, and the priorities of the funding entity.
Kenya Component
The Kenya component aims to contribute to the green growth of Kenya, providing low carbon and lower polluting employment opportunities, increased income, enhanced resilience, and a better quality of life. The programme focuses on increasing the adoption of PUE technologies in agriculture to enhance efficiency and yield, expanding the use of e-mobility solutions, improving energy access for households and SMEs in underserved off-grid communities, and advancing the circular economy and green techologies in Kenya. It will accomplish these goals by offering tailored, concessional capital and technical assistance to innovative companies and business models.
The specific objectives of the Kenya component are:
a) To increase access to modern energy services to underserved communities. b) To increase access to quality productive use of energy (PUE) solutions for MSMEs and agricultural value chains c) To accelerate the growth of reliable, and affordable e-mobility services (mainly 2and 3-wheelers) in Kenya. d) To transform waste management into a more sustainable system that emphasizes, ecosystem restoration, waste recycling, re-use and value reduction, optimizing resource use, and promoting continuous resource circulation.
Ethiopia Component
The Ethiopia component aims to catalyze private sector-led, clean energy access in the agriculture sector in Ethiopia, among others by strengthening financing ecosystems to clean energy access (both demand and supply side) with a view to improve agricultural productivity, food security, and household energy access.
Specifically, the programme seeks to:
a) Accelerate the adoption of Productive Use of Energy (PUE) solutions in agriculture by supporting the deployment of solar-powered agricultural technologies (e.g., irrigation, milling, cold storage, drying) that enhance value addition, reduce post-harvest losses, and promote food system resilience - particularly among smallholder producers and agri-enterprises; b) Improve energy access for households and communities through the expansion of decentralized solar solutions such as Solar Home Systems (SHS) using innovative distribution models (e.g., PayGo, last-mile networks) to reduce energy poverty and reliance on biomass; and c) Strengthen investment readiness and facilitation of fund raising for local, early-stage and growth enterprises to attract private investment through technical assistance, transaction advisory, and matchmaking services.
Regional Africa Component
The Regional component is designed to unlock the potential of digital solutions for accelerating clean energy access and enhancing climate resilience across Sub-Saharan Africa. It addresses critical barriers faced by early and growth-stage enterprises developing and scaling digital transformative innovations in distributed renewable energy (DRE), clean cooking, e-mobility, digital agriculture and the circular economy through the provision of capital and technical support. The project aims to catalyse the development and scaling of digital solutions that expand clean energy access and enhance climate adaptation and mitigation for underserved populations.
The specific objectives of the Regional component are:
a) Improve Clean Energy Access for the Last Mile: By supporting digital solutions that address challenges in distribution, marketing, training, after-sales support, consumer financing, carbon financing, demand stimulation, and operational efficiency, particularly for basic electrification (solar home systems, micro-grids, mini-grids), productive use of energy, clean cooking, and circular economy approaches b) Increase understanding of gender integration approaches for businesses: By supporting business to conduct gender needs assessment and action planning and thus achieve gender integration. c) Enhance Climate Change Mitigation and Adaptation: By fostering digital innovations that support efficient natural resource management and promote adaptive practices within energy systems. d) Promote Energy Efficiency and Sustainable Transitions: By integrating digital tools that aid in the design, implementation, and monitoring of energy efficiency policies and initiatives. This includes promoting new models of energy production, distribution, and consumption that are both inclusive and sustainable. e) Foster Replicability and Systemic Value: By encouraging solutions that are not only innovative but also scalable across multiple markets, ensuring systemic value and broader application beyond initial contexts.
